chapter: Chords, recordings and his own groups
title: Co-leading on 52nd Street; rehearsals; Clyde Hart and Jimmy Butts
summary: He co-led with Ted Briggs, did not rehearse his groups, and says Jimmy Butts stayed longest, with Clyde Hart off and on.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Did you play as a sideman at all after you left Art Tatum, on 52nd Street?

Once. I wasn't a sideman, I was a co-leader with a guy named Teddy Briggs -- Riggs -- Teddy Briggs? ... He was a saxophone player and he knew I worked down there a lot and he got a gig and he offered me partnership to share and get the guys playin' behind him. I think his name was Ted.
How did you rehearse your groups?
We didn't rehearse. We were too far away...
Who stayed with you the longest? Clyde Hart was your regular piano player, right.
I think Jimmy Butts, bass player. Clyde was off and on. Clyde was there -- low key -- quiet like me...
Do you remember Hot Lips Page much?
... Not much ... Hurricane club ... Nothin' special.
